{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABh8yvtA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhLUq80", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 136, "title": "Redesign the WonderSwan web player layout using the streamlined snes-rust UI as reference", "body": "## Problem

The current WonderSwan player works, but its UI spreads basic actions across a large dark player card, a separate playback toolbar, a separate sound row, a console selector above the screen, and a Settings / Help modal containing frequently used display options. The screen competes with surrounding chrome, particularly on mobile.

The same author's [snes-rust browser player](https://takahirox.github.io/snes-rust/) offers a clearer, simpler visual hierarchy: light page background, prominent dark game-screen region, compact playback/audio/display toolbar, separate cartridge slot, lightweight header help, and responsive touch-controller placement. Use its **layout and interaction principles** as a reference for WonderSwan, without copying SNES-specific functionality or introducing unnecessary framework dependencies.

This is a **frontend UI/UX and responsive layout redesign**. It must not change the emulator core, video pixels, CPU timing or save formats.

## Expected outcome

Make `wonderswan-rust` visually and operationally consistent with the streamlined `snes-rust` player:

1. A restrained **light/off-white page**, one quiet accent color, readable dark text and generous but efficient whitespace. The **game display itself remains dark** and visually dominant; avoid the current oversized all-dark outer panel.
2. A compact header with **wonderswan-rust**, **Help**, and a working **GitHub repository link**.
3. At desktop/tablet widths, a **wide game-screen region on the left** and a small **cartridge/console panel on the right**; a single coherent control toolbar directly beneath them. Do not let long filenames or changing status text resize the screen.
4. A clearly labeled cartridge area with the current local filename or **No ROM loaded**, one primary **Load ROM** action, and a **Console** selector for WonderSwan / WonderSwan Color / SwanCrystal. There must be **no bundled demo, ROM catalog, remote downloads or new cartridge-selection modal**.
5. Consolidated controls immediately below the game: **Play/Pause, Restart, compact Mute + volume, Display effect selector and Fullscreen**. Keep the existing display choices **Clean, LCD Light, LCD Authentic and Retro CRT**, and keep **Retro CRT as the new-user default**. An explicit saved display preference must still take precedence; retain the current WebGL failure fallback to Clean.
6. On narrow and touch screens, keep the actual game image as large as practical while arranging the two WonderSwan **X/Y direction keypads plus A/B/Start**, cartridge entry and toolbar predictably. Preserve both horizontal cartridges and the rotated **144×224 portrait presentation**, including fullscreen and touch use.

This should be a useful, polished, **minimal game-first player**, not a pixel-for-pixel port of the SNES implementation.

## Context and reproduction

### Independent layout reference

- [snes-rust `web/index.html`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/index.html): header Help/GitHub, game screen, compact toolbar, cartridge slot, touch controls.
- [snes-rust `web/style.css`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/style.css): light page and dark display, desktop two-column grid, compact volume/display controls, phone portrait/landscape placement, safe-area and fullscreen rules.
- [snes-rust `web/app.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/app.js): interaction structure for playback, ROM selection, display settings and focus.
- The SNES project's included ROM/demo picker, L/R and four face buttons, gameplay controller maps and ROM fetches are **not applicable** to WonderSwan and **must not be added**. Reuse concepts, not its hardware-specific behavior, code or assets.

### Current WonderSwan integration points (inspect latest `main` first)

- [`web/index.html`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/index.html): `.brand`, `.stage`, `#player`, `.player-heading`, `#display`, `#screen-presentation`, `#screen`, `#screen-effect`, `#empty-state`, `#controls`, `.sound-controls`, `#touch-controls`, `#debug-panel`, `#help`. Retain logical accessibility labels and existing IDs when practical to avoid gratuitous integration breakage.
- [`web/src/style.css`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/src/style.css): current dark palette, 946px player card, separate sound row, CSS `rotate(-90deg)` for vertical carts, fullscreen layout, 375px touch rules. Replace the overarching layout and theme coherently; **do not change the shader's image geometry or crop the original pixels**.
- [`web/src/main.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/src/main.ts): local file input, model changes, `setRunning`, focus/key state, keyboard/touch handling, sound activation, display selection, Debug Mode, `sizeScreen()`, ResizeObserver and fullscreen lifecycle. Update event wiring/selectors only as needed; preserve the real behavior and local-file-only security.
- [`web/src/display.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/src/display.ts) and [`web/src/audio.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/src/audio.ts) should keep their algorithms, output contracts, fallback and saved settings. The task is layout/affordances rather than shader/audio rewrites.
- [README UI/UX principles](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/README.md#uiux): **Keep it simple; Show, don't tell; Intuitive and predictable**. Follow [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md) and [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md).
- Existing [Issue #100](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/issues/100) tracks a **Chrome 157 LCD portrait corner** difference. Do not claim this layout redesign fixes that issue or weaken pixel assertions to disguise it.

### Layout and interaction specification

**A. Header and desktop hierarchy**

- Use a lightweight typographic header with title left, an accessible Help affordance and GitHub link right. Move instructional prose and less-used RTC/Debug controls into a compact Help/Settings surface; retain accessible control labels and keyboard/Escape focus behavior.
- Prefer a simple grid/flex layout: **screen (main region)** + **cartridge slot/console selection (secondary region)**, followed by a **single inline responsive toolbar**. Let the screen grow within the native ratio; avoid fixed-width panels causing horizontal scroll.
- Give the cartridge panel a stable footprint, with an ellipsized/wrapped long filename that does not change screen geometry. One primary local **Load ROM** button must remain obvious in the empty state and also usable after inserting a cartridge; avoid duplicate action buttons.
- Avoid unnecessary `Your next game` banners or redundant status labels. Use short state labels such as Ready, Running, Paused and actionable errors only when helpful.

**B. Single controls row**

- Consolidate Pause/Resume, Restart, Mute and Volume slider, live **Display** selector and Fullscreen in one toolbar with sensible wrapping. The existing audio-unlock retry must remain discoverable *only when needed*, and Mute should have an accessible name/state even if rendered as an icon.
- Display selection must be available **without opening Help** and must update a currently running/paused frame without restarting, losing focus/input or changing audio. Preserve preference key `wonderswan:display:v1`, CRT default for unsaved visitors, user selections and Clean fallback.
- Keep the current volume/mute persistence and user-gesture Web Audio unlock. Do not create additional persistent keys or a second mute/volume mechanism.
- The console selector stays clearly separate from aesthetic Display: changing the **physical console model restarts** a loaded cartridge as currently documented, while Display never restarts it. Communicate this distinction without overlong prose.

**C. Mobile, portrait cartridges and fullscreen**

- Narrow portrait phone: layout order should favor **screen → compact playback/display controls → cartridge/console controls → X/Y/A/B/Start touch input** (small adjustments allowed for fit). Ensure the local ROM action remains discoverable before a file is loaded.
- Short landscape phone: where space permits, place touch-control groups on either side of the centered screen and put compact toolbar/cartridge controls below. There are **two independent four-way X/Y groups**, not an SNES D-pad and four face buttons: all X1–X4, Y1–Y4, A/B and Start must stay accessible. If landscape space is genuinely insufficient, use an overflow-safe, clearly reachable alternative rather than reducing targets below usability or hiding controls.
- Support at least 375×812 portrait, 812×375 landscape, narrow desktop/tablet boundaries, and fullscreen; respect mobile safe-area insets, 44px touch targets where practical, wrapping without horizontal overflow, and usable controls when browser UI occupies vertical space.
- Maintain the core's native **224×144** pixels, portrait cartridge `rotate(-90deg)` / **144×224** footprint, square pixels/aspect ratio, clean canvas + WebGL overlay alignment, CRT/LCD shaders, ResizeObserver and fullscreen sizing. The visible picture must not stretch, clip or drift off-center. No display orientation changes to WonderSwan button identities.
- Keep keyboard and multi-touch key union, pressed/released visual state, focus restoration after Help/file selection/fullscreen, and clearing held keys on blur/pause/model changes. Do not interfere with browser/system shortcuts or page scrolling outside the controller.

**D. Notices, errors and auxiliary surfaces**

- Retain `#error`, `#notice`, `#sound-status`, `#display-notice`, `#console-notice`, `#rtc-notice`, initialization retry, Web Audio recovery and save/storage failure messages. Quietly collapse empty notices while **real errors/warnings remain visible, readable, announced and actionable**; do not hide them for visual minimalism.
- Move secondary Help, controls reference, RTC options and Debug Mode out of the primary gameplay area. Debug Mode remains **off by default** with no loss of recorded diagnostic details, and must not cause mobile horizontal overflow when enabled.
- Preserve semantic grouping, accessible names, tab order, Escape/close behavior, visible focus ring, color contrast and keyboard-only usage in the new light theme.
- Do not add an SNES-style game library, built-in ROM selector, gamepad support, new Scale selector, save-state feature, color theme switch, UI framework or dependencies unless strictly necessary to satisfy this Issue.

### Expected structure (illustrative, not literal markup)

```text
wonderswan-rust                               Help   GitHub

+------------------------------------+   +---------------------+
|                                    |   | Cartridge           |
|          GAME SCREEN               |   | No ROM loaded       |
|                                    |   | [Load ROM]          |
|                                    |   | Console [Crystal v] |
+------------------------------------+   +---------------------+
[Play/Pause] [Restart] [Mute] [Volume---] [Display: CRT v] [Fullscreen]

[Error/warning only when needed]      [Touch X/Y/A/B/Start on touch devices]
```

On narrow screens, reflow these regions into a usable single-column / short-landscape arrangement, not a smaller literal desktop grid.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] The public-player frontend has a cohesive **light, spacious, game-first** presentation patterned on snes-rust's information hierarchy: minimal header with working Help/GitHub, dark screen region, stable cartridge/console area and one compact toolbar. No excessive dark outer card or redundant controls remain.
- [ ] On a fresh session the player shows **No ROM loaded**, one clear **Load ROM** route, no bundled game/demo or automatic ROM fetching. Local `.ws`/`.wsc` files still load only client-side; canceling or rejecting a file keeps the prior state. Current cartridge name and console selection stay visible without shifting the screen.
- [ ] Toolbar actions and state transitions work: pause/resume, restart, mute/unmute, volume persistence, blocked-audio retry, fullscreen and all four display effects. **Retro CRT remains default**, existing preferences persist, Clean fallback survives shader failure, and display selection never alters emulated state.
- [ ] Changing Mono/Color/SwanCrystal still applies the existing restart/compatibility semantics and save retention. Moving Console or Display controls does not change their meaning. Cartridge saves, separate console EEPROM records and RTC storage continue to work with existing storage-error notices.
- [ ] Desktop and narrow/portrait/landscape mobile screenshots and layout assertions demonstrate a prominent correctly proportioned screen, stable controls, zero horizontal page overflow and no important action obscured. Cover representative 1280×800 desktop, ~375×812 portrait, ~812×375 landscape, **both horizontal and vertical cartridge orientations**, and fullscreen; test a small representative matrix instead of every Cartesian combination.
- [ ] Touch devices preserve all **X1–X4, Y1–Y4, A/B/Start** inputs with reliable pressed/released states, combined inputs and minimum practical hit areas. Keyboard focus, Help dismissal, file-picker cancellation, fullscreen exit and input clearing still behave correctly. Accessible names/tab order/focus indicators remain meaningful.
- [ ] HTML canvas and WebGL shader output remain aligned for Clean/CRT/LCD in landscape and rotated portrait; native 224×144 buffer and 144×224 display footprint are preserved. Existing known Chrome 157 portrait corner issue #100 is not papered over by altered expectations; document any browser-specific failures accurately.
- [ ] Critical playback, display/audio, invalid-ROM, initialization, storage and runtime errors remain visible and announced. Debug Mode stays optional and off by default. Secondary settings/help are discoverable without crowding the screen.
- [ ] Extend the **existing** production-preview Playwright smoke/compatibility tests for the new layout, using **local source-included CC0 hardware fixture ROMs** from `fixtures/`; assert geometry, visibility, inputs and functional behavior, not just changed labels. Preserve existing meaningful CPU/Wasm/display/audio/save checks without adding unrelated duplicate test suites.
- [ ] Run and record applicable `npm ci`, `npm run build:wasm` (if required for production-preview fixtures), `npm run build`, `npm run test:browser`, `npm run test:compat` and `git diff --check`. Record real pass/fail/skip results, browser versions and any existing known failures. Additional Rust core/fixture builds should be run only when changed files warrant them, per repository test/CI performance rules.
- [ ] Update README's player instructions and any relevant UI screenshots/help text for the new hierarchy. No Rust core modifications, copied SNES emulator functionality, bundled ROMs, new UI framework or unneeded settings/features are introduced.

## Optional validation

- Inspect on physical mobile Safari/Chrome and compare visual balance directly against the [snes-rust public player](https://takahirox.github.io/snes-rust/); these are design/quality checks, not a mandatory human-approval gate.
- Compare screen visibility and touch comfort on additional narrow phones and tablets, including browser address-bar expansion/collapse.

## Required post-merge verification

1. **Pending:** After meeting all pre-merge criteria and merging/closing the Issue, verify the existing `main` GitHub Pages workflow deployed the merge commit successfully and record its run URL. Deployment is **not** a pre-merge check.
2. **Pending:** Open the public [WonderSwan player](https://takahirox.github.io/wonderswan-rust/) unauthenticated and verify the new empty/player layout, loading one original CC0 fixture via local file selection, one narrow/portrait viewport, playback/input and display/audio controls, plus no unexpected ROM/network requests. Distinguish automated browser observations from actual physical-device testing. Log any production-only defect in a linked follow-up Issue instead of reopening a completed task solely for this check.
